column1: # tests/parity.tsv — THE parity record. Single source of truth for
# before/after assertion counts, per suite, per tier.
# Columns (tab-separated; the plan's schema, plus `files` and `task`):
#   suite          the suite name the gate keys on
#   tier           hermetic | fixture
#                  hermetic = no network, no ssh, no remote fixture; runs in the
#                  nix sandbox. fixture = needs the armed remote triple.
#   floor_before   assertions this suite made BEFORE the move. This is the floor
#                  the gate enforces. It is a MEASURED number, never a static
#                  grep of call sites — loops multiply at runtime and a static
#                  count silently under-reports.
#   pass_after     assertions after the move. Filled by the gate as suites land.
#   fail_after     as above.
#   skipped        as above.
#   files          the ledger GROUP names this suite claims. A group is the
#                  basename of the test file that made the assertion
#                  (tests/unit/diag_test.odin -> `diag_test`). A group that NO
#                  row claims is reported UNACCOUNTED by the gate instead of
#                  being folded into some other suite's total — that is how a
#                  new test file becomes visible rather than invisible inside a
#                  passing number.
#   task           the todo that carries this row
#   notes
# THE RULE THIS FILE EXISTS FOR
#   Fewer assertions after the move is a REGRESSION — said out loud, never
#   reported as a green suite.

The 189 old assertion NAMES were diffed against the old dev/state-smoke.sh log: 0 missing, 0 renamed. Sections split into one @(test) proc each so `error_count` is per-section and the old shared `any_failed` flag is gone entirely (the plan's save/restore redesign — nothing to wrap because nothing carries a verdict). state_offline_test 65 = 54 `state-offline` rules (names diffed 1:1, 0 missing) + 7 per-battery 'the window really was stripped' checks + 3 ADDITIVE (round-trip exact, no TERM/TTY/TERMINFO in the window, offline transcript guard). state_surface_test 13 = the 12 grep_absent checks + the ISC-A-3 whole-src sweep, with `//` comments stripped BEFORE matching (blind, mirroring `sed 's,//.*,,'`) so the prose that documents each rule cannot itself violate it. state_safety_test 2 = the real `herdr session list` byte-identical across a full driven battery, + 1 ADDITIVE non-emptiness guard (two EMPTY lists are byte-identical too, so the equality needs a body). OFFLINE MECHANICS: the old run was `env -i PATH=/nonexistent HERDR_ENV=1 HERDR_SESSION=...` as a child process. A child cannot reuse the ledger (it tallies, the parent is silent), so the swap is done in the process that owns the ledger: all-distinct-key snapshot into a .bss byte pool -> refuse-to-strip if it does not fit -> clear_env + 3 vars -> run -> restore -> verify key-by-key. Note core:os's `_environ` duplicates its leading entry on this toolchain (n=180 over 178 keys), so every count/compare here is DISTINCT-KEY based, not entry based. SUPPORT REQUEST (SUPPORT-ENV-MU): a mutex in tests/support that EVERY environment mutation in every suite takes. Each offline proc here holds its own ST_ENV_MU, which serialises the offline file against itself but CANNOT see the theme suite's XDG_WRITE_MU — a per-file mutex only covers the files that remember to take it, and a theme XDG swap live while this window has HOME unset would target the developer's real config. ODIN_TEST_THREADS=1 (plan-mandated for the unit binary) is what keeps this safe today; the shared mutex is what would make it structural. RCH-3/RCH-4 PINNED INTACT, no shortfall: {Mode selection} has rows but NO highlight; 16 unclaimed keys leave the filter EMPTY (the inverted R2 test); Enter there CREATES and never targets; KEY_DELETE decodes to backspace and removes whole runes in every filter AND edit state; no Command ever targets `default` across 128 adversarial probes. `only_created` cleanup is not part of this suite (0 occurrences in the old state suite) — it belongs to app/T10. KNOWN, NOT OURS: theme_hygiene_test emits one `%!(EXTRA <UNSET>)` line. If T15 gives suites SHARED log files, gate rule 7 (`%!` sweep) will pin that on whichever suite shares the log. Per-suite logs keep it where it belongs.

column1: # WHY `pty` IS ITS OWN TIER AND NOT `hermetic`
# Verified (D-T15): a real pty WORKS in the nix sandbox -- /dev/ptmx is
# present and a child can take a controlling terminal. So this tier belongs in
# `nix flake check` and does NOT need the armed remote fixture.
# It is still not the hermetic tier. It requires a device node hermetic tests
# must never depend on, and a sandbox built without /dev/ptmx has to be able to
# exclude these four rows WITHOUT taking the whole hermetic suite down. Folding
# them into `hermetic` would couple them: one missing device node, and every
# hermetic row fails for a reason that has nothing to do with what it tests.
# THE GATE NO LONGER DEFAULTS AN UNKNOWN TIER TO HERMETIC. It refuses the row
# out loud. Until this change, a typo in the tier column -- or a new tier the
# gate had not been taught, exactly like `pty` before now -- was silently filed
# under hermetic. With tiering load-bearing for T15 that is the worst possible
# failure: the tier column would look authoritative while being a guess.
# VERIFIED BY SCRIPT, NOT BY HAND:  bash tests/tools/hscheck/check_parity_arith.sh
# That script re-reads these rows and reconciles them against their origin. If you
# change a floor, it will fail until you update the origin list in the SAME commit.
# The comment below is a rendering of what the script computes; the script is the
# authority. Hand-maintained totals in a file that changes every time a lane lands
# are not verification, they are a claim that goes stale quietly.
# Verified 1862 = 1478 hermetic + 254 pty + 130 fixture. Perturbing any row
# makes the script exit 1; an unknown tier value makes it name the tier.
#  fixture  :  88 + 27 + 15
#  pty      :  67 + 27 + 73 + 51  (lane P, EXISTS)                =  218
#           +  36  (theme pty, DEFERRED -- tests not yet written)  =   36
#             pty tier total                                      =  254
#    = 1544 (armed bash baseline)
#    +   54 (T2: diag 10 + keyhints 44)
#    +   10 (T2 keyhints raised 44 -> 54: the explicit app.State
#           coverage walk added this session, so the +10 is locked in and a
#           future deletion of it is caught rather than absorbed)
#    +  218 (lane P: width 67 + ffi 27 + screen 73 + driver 51)
#    +   36 (theme tty work, RESERVED not yet delivered)
#  Every number for work that EXISTS was re-measured through the gate with
#  max-per-group by lane S, not copied from a lane's self-report. Lane P's
#  reported 218 reproduced exactly (67/27/73/51, 38 tests, 0 fail, 0 skip).
#  The naive line-sum over the same run reads 7999 -- which is why the
#  max-per-group rule is not optional.
#  THE 36 IS NOT YET REAL. The `theme`/pty row claims `theme_pty_*`, groups
#  no file produces yet. Running the gate against it TODAY fails rule 3b
#  ("this row claims no group present in the log"), and that is the correct
#  outcome: a reserved floor must fail rather than pass vacuously, so the row
#  cannot quietly become a permanent exemption. Flagging it because
#  `--tier=pty` is therefore RED until that work lands, by design -- do not
#  "fix" it by lowering the floor.
#  Read the `diag` and `keyhints` rows together: both ADD. Neither steals from
#  `app` or `ui`. Nothing in the 1544 was removed to pay for them; if a later
#  task deletes a duplicated battery, it must subtract from the row that is
#  losing it in the SAME diff, or this file stops meaning anything.
# KNOWN PRE-EXISTING FLAKE (NOT introduced by T2; recorded, threshold NOT
# loosened). The `idle <= 2 clock ticks over 5 s` assertion in the tui suite
# fails intermittently under machine load. Measured on a binary built from
# 2a9fb85 -- BEFORE any RCH-8 rename -- 2 of 5 runs failed at 9 and 29 ticks;
# on the post-rename binary, 1 of 3 at ~21 ticks. An identifier-only rename
# cannot change CPU behaviour, so this is load sensitivity in the measurement,
# pre-dating this work. The threshold above stays at 2 UNCHANGED. It should be
# made robust (measure the herdr process's own ticks, not the whole machine's,
# or widen with justification in a diff) by whoever owns T12 -- but that is a
# decision, not a green-making tweak.
